root_cause.text: The function intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr performs a container_of operation on the event's PMU assuming it is an x86 hybrid PMU, but software events (non-x86 events) can be present in the same group, leading to out-of-bounds memory reads.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "Auto counter reload may have a group of events with software events present within it. The software event PMU isn't the x86_hybrid_pmu and a container_of operation in intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr (via the hybrid helper) could cause out of bound memory reads." The patch adds a guard `if (is_x86_event(sibling))` before calling `intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr` on sibling events.

Calls intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr on each sibling event during the loop. Siblings can be software events that are not x86 hybrid, triggering the same container_of vulnerability when processed.
Controls whether siblings are processed. Without a check on event type, this condition allows the vulnerable loop to execute even when siblings include non-x86 software events.
Iterates over all sibling events, including non-x86 events. This macro directly enables the vulnerable calls to intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr on events that may not have a hybrid PMU.

A conditional that may lead to additional processing of events not checked for PMU type. While not directly calling the function, it influences the control flow and could expose other events to the same vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr is added in this commit and calls hybrid(event->pmu, acr_cause_mask64) without verifying that event->pmu is an x86 hybrid PMU. In the hw_config() code, the second round calls this function for all siblings, including non-x86 events (software events), as seen in the loop 'for_each_sibling_event(sibling, leader) intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr(sibling, idx++, cause_mask);'. There is no is_x86_event check in that path, so a software event's pmu will be mis-cast, causing out-of-bounds memory reads. The first round only skips non-x86 siblings for setting counter constraints, but does not prevent them from being passed to intel_pmu_set_acr_caused_constr later.
